citation.title: A deep Convolutional Neural Network for topology optimization with strong generalization ability
citation.authors: Yiquan Zhang, Bo Peng, Xiaoyi Zhou, Cheng Xiang, Dalei Wang

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The CNN reduced mean computation time from 3.913 s with SIMP to 0.001 s per case, while reported average compliance and volume-fraction errors were 4.16% and 0.13%.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 5 reports average conventional time 3.913 s and proposed time 0.001 s; 3.913 ÷ 0.001 = 3913. The ML time is rounded to 0.001 s.
claim.alternatives: Conclusion qualitatively says the CNN solves the problem in negligible time; abstract also says it generalizes to unseen boundary conditions with lower accuracy.

baseline.implementation: 88-line MATLAB topology optimization code (Andreassen et al. 2011)
baseline.hardware_classical: Intel Core i7-8700K CPU and NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti GPU system (Section 5)
baseline.hardware_ml: Intel Core i7-8700K CPU and NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti GPU system (Section 5)
baseline.training_time: not stated; excluded from reported computation time (Section 5)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; excluded from reported computation time (Section 5)
baseline.quality_metric: Finite-element compliance error, pixel-value error, and volume-fraction error (Table 1)
baseline.quality_gap: Average compliance error 4.16% and volume-fraction error 0.13%; disconnected samples are excluded from averages (Table 1 footnote).

R1.evidence: Section 5 and Table 1 compare timed designs and report average compliance error of 4.16% and volume-fraction error of 0.13%; the article also reports disconnected cases separately.

R2.evidence: Section 5 gives average times and a shared CPU/GPU system, but no solver details or evidence establishing R2(a)–(e).

R3.evidence: Section 5 explicitly excludes dataset-generation and neural-network training costs from the timing comparison and gives no amounts or break-even analysis.

R4.evidence: Sections 5–6 report compliance and volume-fraction errors and count structural disconnections (4.12% in the cantilever test set; Tables 1–2).

reporting.n_test_cases: 8,000 cantilever cases; 8,000 each for simply supported and continuous beams (Sections 5–6)

notes: Training and dataset preparation costs are excluded; no public code or data release is stated. Source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1901.07761
